originality.rationale: The prior constant-step OGDA results imply neither the two-period product characteristic polynomial nor its global stability region. The only directly related adaptive source uses a different safeguarded update, so its guarantees do not apply to naive step scaling. The accessible literature and record comparisons did not identify a covering claim; a possible broader variable-coefficient multistep implication remains a disclosed priority risk.
residual_risks: An older general variable-coefficient two-step or switched-systems stability theorem might contain this period-two criterion as an implicit special case; this was not independently eliminated.
The analysis is for naively scaled OGDA only; applying it to guarded adaptive GRAAL or arbitrary OGDA variable-step definitions would be incorrect.
Independent priority and mathematical validation were not performed.

value.rationale: Individually stable OGDA steps do not guarantee convergence under naive variable-step reuse of past gradients, even as both steps vanish. The result provides a sharp, nontrivial relative-step frontier 2±sqrt(3) and exact all-scale Floquet stability criterion for a canonical game; these identify a principled risk in time-varying historical-gradient methods rather than an arbitrary numerical counterexample.
